title: Unpacking the Complex Link Between Messaging and Perceived Social Support in Emerging Adulthood: Key Contextual Factors
abstract: Messaging, often considered an interactive form of communication, is believed to enhance emerging adults’ well-being by fostering social support. However, findings, including meta-reviews, remain inconsistent. This experience sampling study among emerging adults ( n = 108, Mage = 22.29, SDage = 1.66), therefore, examines three key factors that may shape this relationship: monitoring of message cues, communication partner tie strength, and conversation valence. Results show no general between- or within-person associations between messaging and social support. Additionally, cue monitoring, tie strength, and conversation valence did not moderate the messaging–support link. However, both tie strength and conversation valence did directly predict social support at the within-person level, suggesting that the quality of interactions, rather than frequency, is more essential. Overall, this study highlights the importance of contextual factors in understanding the nuanced effects of messaging.
